properties.name: Feedback sources are triaged in a stated order: dev_storyflow first, Alex level with it, music_graph after
properties.statement:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16, stated in passing while asking for a triage sweep: "dev_storyflow is a higher priority" and "any un-addressed feedback from my brother should be addressed — it is right up there in importance next to dev_storyflow". Recorded because it is a STANDING ordering, not a one-off instruction for that sweep, and because a future session with three logs and finite attention will otherwise re-derive it wrongly or read them in whatever order they were handed over.

THE ORDER: dev_storyflow first — Alex level with it — music_graph after.

WHY IT IS NOT ARBITRARY, inferred and marked as inference rather than as his stated reasoning: dev_storyflow is the fleet Anthony runs himself, so its log is his own usage at scale and arrives fastest; Alex is the SECOND HUMAN USER, and a second user's friction is the only evidence reflow2 has about anyone who did not build it; music_graph is a single consumer project whose reports, while excellent, have so far concentrated on one surface (restore and setup). ⚠️ HE DID NOT SAY THIS — he stated the order and not the grounds, and a later session should not quote the reasoning back to him as his.

WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN, since a priority order is easy to over-read: it is not a quality ranking. music_graph's F23 was the most consumer-blocking defect of the whole increment and was fixed first, before this ordering was stated. Priority here is about which log to READ when there is not time for all of them, not about whose findings matter.

📌 `enforced: false` DELIBERATELY, and the reason is that no check is possible: nothing in the graph knows which log a session read, or in what order. So this is guidance for a reader and must not be raised as an unverified enforced rule.

⚠️ THIS NODE WAS CREATED WRONG THE FIRST TIME AND THE ERROR IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED: it was written with `enforcement: "advisory"`, a property the schema does not declare. It was ACCEPTED AND STORED, echoed back, and the enforcement gap fired anyway — which is what exposed it. See `fact:defect-an-undeclared-property-is-stored-without-complaint`.

AN INPUT TO AN OPEN QUESTION: `dec:idea-is-there-a-feedback-intake-skill-and-is-it-a-router` asks whether reflow2 should have a feedback skill that routes external input. If that is ever built, THIS is a thing it would need to know and has nowhere to read.
